summary: The hub root fairing rework fixes last review's major. I swept fold_r and fold_l past spread with the built parts: the stop post touches at -1.4 deg (8.25 mm3 at -2, 37.1 at -3), and the nose stays 0.451 mm off the ridge's front corner even at -3 deg, on both sides. The ligament by the lead channel is back to its old stress (max 15.2 MPa, none over 17.5), and only three small fairing minors remain. The project still FAILS on problems that were there before this change: hub_fea, spine_fea and deck_fea, 15 % infill under stress the lattice cannot carry (hub, spine), a zero-clearance rub between the spine's ridge fillet and each hub boss, short aileron leads and about 45 wiring routes through solid parts.

findings.issue: Root fairing (this change): nothing guards the new over-travel clearance. The nose-to-ridge gap (0.451 mm at -3 deg) is now right, but no requirement checks it. clearance_min only samples inside the joint range [0, 70], and hard_stop only compares aft_fuse with the hub. If anyone changes RIDGE_HW, CAP_MAX, STOP_GAP or pivot_x later, it can touch again before the stop and every check will still pass. STATUS.md records this as an open engine gap, which is honest, but it is still open. Note: a hub-vs-spine clearance check would read 0.0 mm today because of the spine fillet / boss rub (separate major below), so that has to be fixed first.
findings.fix: Engine: give clearance_min a 'beyond' pose (or have hard_stop report any third part that touches the moving part before the stop pair does), with a test. Then add hub_r-spine and hub_l-spine clearance requirements >= 0.3 mm at fold -3 deg (and >= 0.5 mm over 0..70).

findings.issue: Root fairing (this change): the nose has a wave in plan view (top render). I measured its reach inboard of the root face: 10.0 mm at x 35-65, down to 6.3 at x 100, back up to 7.7 at x 135, then fading to zero by x 165. The dip is the ridge limit at the ridge front. Aft of that the limit relaxes, because a point closer to the pin swings less, so the reach grows again. The rule is physically correct, but the result is a hump with no purpose on the folded leading edge, and it reads as unintended. This is cosmetic and slightly aerodynamic, not a clearance problem.
findings.fix: Use the running minimum of the ridge limit from x 95 aft (each station takes the smallest limit at or ahead of it). The reach then falls smoothly from 10 to about 6.3 mm and stays level until the fade starts at x 150. hub_l follows (built from the same body).

findings.issue: Root fairing: what still faces the folded flow (carried over, open in STATUS.md). The flat area within 30 deg of square to the wind at 70 deg is 111.7 mm2 by my measurement (designer: 111). Of that, 110.8 mm2 is one face: the bare root strip from the nose's end (x 166) to the collar (x 180.6). At 0 and 35 deg it is 11.3 and 0 mm2. The V keel's 45 deg inboard face (x 130-205, down to z -9.4) is still a ramp under the folded leading edge, and the boss stands about 11 mm proud at the root trailing edge.
findings.fix: Same as last review, now one job: move L.lead_exit so the lead channel stays >= 3.4 mm behind the root face (the spine cover lead slot and the aft_fuse arc slot follow it). Then run the nose on into the collar and wrap it down over the keel for x 130-176. That removes the 111 mm2 strip and the ramp, and adds section depth where hub_fea fails.

findings.issue: hub_fea fails (pre-existing): p99.9 von Mises 24.33 MPa against 17.5 allowed (CF-PETG / SF 2), and 8.14 mm deflection at the root leading edge (14.7, 90, -0.4) against 1.0 mm, 8 times over. The load enters where it should (32 N lift on the spar sockets plus the root moment) and the hot spots are on the load path: the thin root trailing edge into a 20 mm boss held at its pin bore. The aileron lead channel cell at (174, 29.2, -2.4) is as bad as before (39.3 MPa now, 38.0 last time), and the trailing-edge corner behind the pin (210, 39.8, 0.1) peaks at 97 MPa. The fairing change did not move this either way.
findings.fix: Make the section from the rear spar socket to the boss a full-depth box: merge the keel, collar and root nose into one web at least 15-20 mm deep running into the boss. Grow the boss (r 10 -> 13) and the collar. Move the lead channel off the root-face ligament (see the fairing minor). If the deflection is still over 1 mm, bond in a CF plate or tube from the main spar socket to the boss. Do not loosen the 1 mm limit without a cited reason.

findings.issue: hub_l is the mirror image of hub_r (same body, same 6 g load) and has no FEA of its own, so the hub_fea failure (24.33 vs 17.5 MPa, 8.14 vs 1.0 mm) applies to it unchanged.
findings.fix: Fixed by the same hub.py change as hub_r. Re-run hub_fea afterwards. Optionally add a hub_l case so the failure table stops showing it as 'no strength case'.

findings.issue: Infill (pre-existing geometry; the engine check is new, kerf/infill.py). hub_r prints at 15 % infill, so its core is a lattice about 2 % as strong as solid plastic. The FEA puts stress up to 22.7 times that deeper than the 1.68 mm walls, over 34 % of the part's volume, worst near (188.4, 35.5, -5.7): 13.8 MPa mean and 20.3 MPa max within 4 mm. ENGINEERING.md 3b says that stress must stay under the lattice strength. It also means the failing hub_fea numbers are optimistic: they assume a solid core. hub_l is identical.
findings.fix: Add a 100 % infill modifier box over the root block and boss (about x 140-215, y 16-45, full height, including the sector web), or raise the whole hub to >= 60 % infill with more wall loops. Keep the outboard root airfoil and the nose at 15 %. Put it in PRINT_SETTINGS / the 3MF, re-run the build and confirm the infill warning is gone.

findings.issue: spine_fea fails (pre-existing): 53.61 MPa against 16 allowed (3.4 times over), peak 100.6 MPa at (197.8, -26.0, 19.1), and 2.1 mm deflection against 0.5. Each pin is in single shear at the arm, which adds a 5016 N mm moment at the bore. The arm is a 6 mm PETG plate hanging off the ridge, and its two root corners are declared sharp in the hottest zone (utilisation about 4.0).
findings.fix: Re-section the arm: 10-12 mm deep, with a real fillet or gusset down to the ridge. Or put the pin in double shear, or use an aluminium or CF top plate pressed onto the pin. Re-run spine_fea at the same load.

findings.issue: Zero running clearance to each hub boss (pre-existing geometry, found now; this change did not cause it). spine.py runs fillet_inside (r 2) after cutting the r 11 boss holes. The ridge-to-cover cove therefore runs the full ridge length (x 100.3-220.7) out to y +-16 at z -10, and over each boss hole it leaves a 0 to 0.27 mm sliver (6.2 mm2, x 195.4-204.6). The hub boss (r 10 about the pin at y +-26) is tangent to that cove at (200, +-16, -10). I measured exactly 0.000 mm at fold 0, -1.4 and -3 deg, and it is the same at every fold angle because the boss turns about its own axis. ENGINEERING.md asks >= 0.5 mm between moving printed parts over the full range. No check sees it: the sweeps look for overlap volume, and a tangent contact has none. In the print, the boss scrapes a feather edge on every fold. That adds friction on a fold drive already at 6.18 of 7.59 kg cm, and debris near the gear.
findings.fix: In spine.py, exempt the cove inside the boss hole footprint (the keep callback, or cut the boss and lead holes after fillet_inside), so the hole rim stays at r 11, 1 mm off the boss. Add clearance_min hub_r-spine and hub_l-spine >= 0.5 mm over fold_r / fold_l 0..70 so it stays fixed.

findings.issue: Infill (pre-existing geometry; the engine check is new). The spine prints at 15 % infill, and the FEA puts stress up to 39.2 times the lattice strength deeper than the walls, over 17 % of its volume, worst near (203.3, 23.3, 15.2): the arm and ridge round the pin. ENGINEERING.md 3b. The failing spine_fea (solid assumption) is therefore optimistic too.
findings.fix: Add a 100 % infill modifier over both arms and the ridge from x 185 to 220 (or print the spine at 100 %, it is 60 g), as part of the arm re-section.

findings.issue: deck_fea did not run ('PLC Error: A segment and a facet intersect'), so the lower pivot plate (deck) has no strength proof. It carries the same pin bearing couple that overloads the spine arm 3.4 times. The failure table shows aft_fuse at '0 %', which really means 'unknown'.
findings.fix: Clean up the deck and stop-post geometry so it meshes (probably the same sliver and sharp-corner geometry as the corner finding below). Run deck_fea and size the deck and ribs from the result.

findings.issue: 103 sharp inside corners (1281 mm of edge) are neither filleted nor declared, e.g. (226.4, 0, -15.5), (221, 0, -12.5), (218, +-26.2, -72.3). There are also 8 that fillet_inside could not do, near (222, +-27.5..+-12, -24.5) and (210.7, +-8.7, -13). Several are on the deck, keel rib and rear lug, in the pin load path.
findings.fix: Fix the corners that failed (adjust plate edges so a 1.5 mm cove fits) or declare each one with its reason. Fillet the deck-to-rib and rib-to-lug junctions in particular.

findings.issue: The aileron servo leads are too short: ail_r_pwr/sig and ail_l_pwr/sig are declared at 620 mm, but the routed path at full fold plus 15 % slack is 719.9 / 727.5 mm.
findings.fix: Declare about 750 mm leads, or a 150-200 mm extension per servo (catalog entry with its source), and put it in the BOM and WIRING.md.

findings.issue: About 45 wiring routes pass through solid parts instead of holes or channels: main and phases through fwd_fuse, motor_mount and the battery; servo, GPS and tail leads through fwd_fuse, aft_fuse, spine, hatch, tail_mount and hub_r; aileron leads through wing_r1/r2 and wing_l1/l2 (127-137 mm3 each), even though the wings have a 4 mm lead channel. WIRING.md cannot be built as written.
findings.fix: Route every run through features that exist (the wing and hub lead channel, the bulkhead pass-through, the spine GPS hole). Where none exists, add a hole or channel in the part that owns the wall. Re-check until there are 0 'runs through' problems.

findings.issue: Aerodynamics at full spread: the ridge front is a vertical face about 28 mm wide and 17 mm tall, chamfered only on its top edge, square to the flow in the 32 mm channel between the two root noses ahead of x 100.
findings.fix: Give the ridge front a wedge or ogive nose in plan view (|y| 14 tapering to ~4 over ~25 mm), keeping the GPS pad and the front bolts inside it. The nose's ridge limit is taken at the ridge's front corner, so a tapered front only adds clearance.

findings.issue: Print setup (pre-existing, partly addressed). The new assembly_note (in ASSEMBLY.md) covers sanding the nose. The rest of the airfoil block still floats about 15 mm above the bed on tree supports (30.7 % of the surface), on the most stressed printed part. Correction to my last review: I wrote that the nose costs about 8 g per hub at 40 % infill. The hub prints at 15 %, so that mass point is withdrawn. The 0.3 mm lip is accepted as harmless.
findings.fix: Set support interface layers and a 0.2 mm top Z distance for CF-PETG on hub_r/hub_l, and extend the assembly_note to the whole lower surface.

findings.issue: Overbuilt in a mass-limited aircraft: fwd_fuse is 183.5 g of PLA working at 6 % of allowable with 100 % of its volume cold; tail_mount 3 %, motor_mount 4 %. AUW 1590 of 1650 g, wing loading 87.6 of 95 g/dm2, stall 41.4 of 45 km/h.
findings.fix: Remove idle material, not walls: lightening windows in the battery-bay side walls (clear of the hatch ledges and strap slots), and lower infill at the reported cold zones. Then re-run fuse_fea and tail_fea.

findings.issue: The 4 M3 horn-screw holes leave only 71 % of the ring material near the tooth roots (pinion_l the same), while Lewis bending already runs at 13.58 of 16 MPa (85 %).
findings.fix: Check whether the screw circle can move 0.5 mm inward on the horn pattern (catalog). If not, make the pinion 2 mm wider.

findings.issue: The 4 sweep-servo screws on each side need a ball-end 2.5 mm key (a straight key hits the servo body), and the sweep_servo insert holes have 88 % edge material.
findings.fix: Put 'ball-end 2.5 mm key' in the ASSEMBLY tools list, or move the servo tab shelf so a straight key reaches.

findings.issue: Walls below 1.2 mm: elevator 0.93, rudder 0.86, ail_r/l 1.02-1.03, hatch 1.01, tail_mount 1.12 mm.
findings.fix: Thicken the hinge-line webs and trailing-edge regions to >= 1.2 mm, or confirm they are single-line skins and say so in each part's docstring.

findings.issue: DESIGN.md is still out of date: its requirements table says AUW <= 1150 g, wing loading <= 65 g/dm2, stall <= 40 km/h, T/W >= 0.7, flight >= 25 min and hand launch, but project.yaml checks 1650 / 95 / 45 / 0.45 / 12 and a bungee launch. 'Assembly order' and 'Risks / measure first' are still placeholders.
findings.fix: Update the table to the yaml values with the reason (Spencer's decision, commit 94fe2e3), and fill Assembly order / Risks from ASSEMBLY.md and report.json.

findings.issue: Exports: the KiCad symbols are now installed, but ERC still does not run ('no pin table in catalog/pins.json' for fc, esc and gps). The URDF still has joint/link name collisions (ail_l, ail_r, elevator, rudder).
findings.fix: Add the F405-WMO, Skywalker 40A and M9N pin tables to catalog/pins.json (with sources) and re-check. Rename the URDF joints (e.g. j_ail_l) in the URDF writer.
